title: openai-chat-completions: parity for streaming, function-calls, roles, stop/logprobs, and response formatting
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions OpenAI compatibility layer to parity for a set of API behaviors: explicit role handling, stop token semantics across streaming + non-streaming, streaming logprobs propagation, stable function/tool calling over streamed responses, and improved response formatting (structured output preservation). Motivation: customers integrating with OpenAI client libraries expect matching semantics for migration and SDK parity tests (ENG-5791). This PR unifies edge cases we saw in integration tests and production canaries (streaming function calls dropped final tokens; stop was ignored for some streaming paths; streaming logprobs were incomplete).

Changes made (high level):
- Align role ordering and validation with OpenAI: normalize role aliases (e.g., assistant/system/user), enforce JSON schema for input messages.
- Stop token handling: implement consistent stop truncation in the streaming pipeline and non-streaming path so that tokens after a stop sequence are not emitted and callbacks receive a final truncated chunk.
- Streaming logprobs: surface partial token logprobs in the SSE stream, and emit final aggregated logprobs in the summary event to match OpenAI semantics.
- Function/tool calling over streaming: stabilize function call boundaries so tools are called after the final function call token is emitted; add buffering to avoid partial JSON function call bodies on early flushes.
- Response formatting: preserve structured_output flag and ensure JSON/structured outputs are emitted atomically at the end of the response; fallback to best-effort structured parsing for legacy models.
- Tests and canaries: added end-to-end transfer tests for streaming function calls, unit tests for stop/truncation, and added a perf canary to validate latency regressions.

Files changed (high level):
- server/openai_compat/handler.go: compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions (validation + parameter mapping).
- server/openai_compat/streaming_manager.go: fixes for stop handling and SSE framing.
- runtime/stream/stream_manager.go: buffering and flush policy updates to prevent partial function-call bodies.
- runtime/formatters/chat_formatter.go: structured output preservation and final emission logic.
- sdk/python/openai_compat.py: parity shim for client-facing behavior and unit test harness.
- tests/integration/openai_parity/streaming_function_calls_test.go: e2e tests.
- tests/unit/stop_handling_test.go: micro tests for stop sequences.
- perf/canaries/streaming_function_call_canary.yaml: canary config.

Commit summary:
- Normalize roles + validation: 4a7c2d3
- Stop-aware streaming flush + tests: 9f12b8a
- Streaming logprobs & summary event: b3e4f09
- Function call buffering + stability: d0f7a11
- Structured output atomic emit: 5c9e2b4
- SDK parity shim + tests: 7a11d2f

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Performance canary added
- [x] Docs updated (internal OpenAI-compat notes)

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids touching the core tokenizer or model runtime; it focuses on the API surface and streaming infrastructure. Performance impact was measured in the perf canary and is within our SLOs (p50 unchanged, p95 +5–10ms due to buffering). If we see higher tail latency in high-concurrency workloads we will iterate on the flush policy (follow-up: ENG-5830).
review_comments: Samir: Please add a unit test that includes overlapping stop sequences (e.g., \"\n\" and \"END\"). I hit an edge-case in the local runner.
Ava: Added stop_handling_test.go covering overlapping sequences and updated handler.go accordingly.
Elena: The buffering looks good; can you add a small comment near the flush timeout explaining the 50ms tradeoff?
Ava: Comment added + linked to ENG-5830 for potential tuning.
Markus: Verified e2e canary results in staging — p95 latency +8ms which is acceptable. Approved.

release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: role normalization, consistent stop behavior in streaming and non-streaming paths, streaming logprobs propagation, stabilized streaming function/tool calling, and improved structured response formatting. Added tests and a perf canary.
notes_for_release: Customers using the OpenAI compatibility layer should see improved parity for streaming behavior and function calls. No action required. If you rely on previously observed partial streamed function-call JSON bodies, please switch to the final function_call event handling (see internal OpenAI-compat docs).
changelog_entry: feat(openai-compat): match OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics for roles, stop, logprobs, streaming function calls, and structured output. Adds tests and canary.
